candidates.name: Grossmünster
candidates.content: Old Romanesque church, symbol of reformed Zurich, where reformer Huldrych Zwingli was appointed the people's priest in 1519. Go up the tower for a great view of Zurich, though the stairs can be quite small and steep.

candidates.name: Landesmuseum
candidates.hours: Tue-Sun 10:00–17:00 and most public holidays including Mon, Thu until 19ː00
candidates.content: This is the place to go if you want to learn more about the history of Switzerland. There are permanent exhibitions on history, archaeology and art. Changing temporary exhibitions usually revolve around Swiss topics.

candidates.name: Kunsthaus
candidates.price: Fr. 16/11 for the permanent collection. Free on Wednesdays
candidates.content: Zurich's most famous art museum. The collection includes works from many Swiss artists, such as the sculptures of Alberto Giacometti or the paintings of Ferdinand Hodler. There are also major works from international artists on di

candidates.name: Pavillon Le Corbusier
candidates.content: This is the last building designed by the Swiss architect le Corbusier. The Pavillon was built after his death as a museum dedicated to his work. Access to the building has long been difficult and expensive, also due to a legal fi

candidates.name: Zoological Museum
candidates.content: Showcases the zoological collection of the university of Zurich. The first floor has local fauna whereas the lower floor has animals from all over the world.

candidates.name: Fraumünster
candidates.content: Old Gothic church (former convent) with window paintings made by Marc Chagall. No photos or videos allowed inside.

candidates.name: Niederdorf
candidates.content: The old town offers beautiful alleys, restaurants and shopping mainly aimed at younger consumers. In the evenings, people visit the Niederdorf's many bars.

candidates.name: Johann Jacobs Museum
candidates.content: A museum that describes the complex history of global trade routes and goods and the culture around them.

candidates.name: FIFA World Football Museum
candidates.content: Explores the world of football and the FIFA.

candidates.name: Villa Patumbah
candidates.content: Stunning 19th century villa, which houses an architectural history museum (Heimatschutzzentrum).

candidates.name: Lindenhof
candidates.content: The hill in the heart of the old town. A beautiful view of the city and one time location of a Roman fort.

candidates.name: Schanzengraben
candidates.content: A small canal that used to be part of the city fortifications between Limmat and Sihl. From the main station, go to Gessnerallee, find the stairways down to the tiny creek, and walk all the way to the lake.

candidates.name: Langstrasse
candidates.content: Red light district of Zurich, with more drug dealers and police than usual, but interesting because even this most notorious spot in Switzerland is so clean and safe. The area is the most overtly multicultural spot of the town. At

candidates.name: Friedhof Fluntern
candidates.content: cemetery with lots of famous people most notably James Joyce who lived in Zurich for quite some time, the writer Elias Canetti and a few nobel prize winners are also buried there

candidates.name: Zoo
candidates.price: Fr. 26 for adults (Fr. 19 for those under 25)
candidates.content: With the new Masoala Rainforest Hall, the Zoo is really worth a visit!

candidates.name: China Garden
candidates.content: This small but beautiful Chinese garden was offered to the city of Zurich by the Chinese city of Kunming as symbol of gratitude after Zurich helped Kunming with technical knowledge. It can be very well combined with a stroll along

candidates.name: Bahnhofstrasse
candidates.content: One of the busiest and best-known shopping streets in the world. Highly refined. Certainly a must-see for every tourist in Zurich!

candidates.name: Zurich West
candidates.content: This modern quarter used to be an industrial one, but modern urban developments made it into a centre of vibrant night life.

candidates.name: Rietberg Museum
candidates.content: This is one of the largest art museums in Switzerland, administered by the City of Zurich. Its focus lies on the traditional and contemporary arts and cultures of Asia, Africa, the Americas, and Oceania. The complex consists of th

candidates.name: Lake Promenade
candidates.content: Especially during summer, the lake is a beautiful place to spend the evening or the weekend. Starting from Bellevue, the boardwalk goes for about three kilometers along the lake towards Tiefenbrunnen. About halfway from Bellevue t

candidates.name: Polybahn
candidates.price: Fr. 1.20, free with Zürich Card or a valid ZVV ticket for Zone 110
candidates.hours: Operates Mon-Fri 06:45–19:15, Sat 07:30–14:00, closed on Sun and public holidays
candidates.content: A 19th-century funicular, up the steep hill for a fine view. Starts at tram station Central and goes up to the ETH. Nice terrace up there. During the week, the student cafeteria below the terrace is also open to the public.

candidates.name: Uetliberg
candidates.price: Free with Zürich Card or a valid ZVV ticket for the Zones 110, 154, and 155 (costs 4 zones). CHF 2.50 to go up the observation tower
candidates.content: A hill overlooking Zurich. You can hike up, or take a train from the "SZU" part of the main station on the S10, which takes about 20 minutes from Zurich HB. Enjoy the 360-degree view from a tall viewing tower (not for vertigo suff

candidates.name: Caliente Festival
candidates.content: The largest Latin festival in Europe. Held every year in early July. Try all types of Latin American food and listen to samba, merengue & co. Huge crowds.

candidates.name: Züri Fäscht
candidates.content: A weekend festival celebrating Zurich, which occurs every 3 years (last held 7-9 July 2023). It is visited by around 2 million people. In 2023, the committee that had so far organized the Züri Fäscht cancelled their involvement wi

candidates.name: Opernhaus
candidates.content: The Zurich Opera shows frequently changing productions of world famous operas with top artists. As with the Schauspielhaus, students get a big last-minute discount. The best seats costs Fr. 45 for students.

candidates.name: Schauspielhaus
candidates.content: Zurich's Schauspielhaus is one of the most important theatres in the German speaking part of Europe. The Schauspielhaus has several locations, the most important one being the Pfauen. Students can get really cheap last minute tick

candidates.name: Oberer/Unterer Letten
candidates.content: If you go to Zurich during summer take your swimwear with you. The clean river at both the public river baths "Oberer Letten" (mainly youngsters) and "Unterer Letten" (also families) is used by the locals to cool down after hot da

candidates.name: trip on the Zürichsee
candidates.content: With one of the two old steam ships. There are a few different routes you can choose from, which will vary mainly in the distance. Journeys usually start from Bürkliplatz. Steam ships operate between April and mid-October.

candidates.name: Street Parade
candidates.content: The biggest open air techno rave in Europe. It happens one day each year on the second Saturday of August, during which trucks which function as mobile soundsystems ("Love mobiles") start driving along the lake side, starting from

candidates.name: Sechseläuten (Sächsilüüte)
candidates.content: On the third Monday of April, the guilds of Zurich celebrate their traditional spring festival with the burning of the snow man (Böögg). A procession of several hundreds of people with historical guild costumes and horses takes pl

candidates.name: Zürcher Theater Spektakel
candidates.hours: Last two weeks of Aug, from 17:00
candidates.content: A festival for the performing arts. Held along the lake on the Landiwiese near Rote Fabrik and features a number of free performances. Usually in August.

candidates.name: Rote Fabrik
candidates.content: An old silk factory converted to a centre of youth culture and art in the 1980s. The Red Factory became one of the most exciting parts of cultural life. An artists' coop, a couple of kilometers south, form along the west bank of L

candidates.name: Tonhalle Maag
candidates.content: During the renovation of the Tonhalle concert house the internationally renowned classical orchestra, the Tonhalle Orchester Zürich, plays at the intermediately built Tonhalle Maag concert hall. From season 2019/20, Paavo Järvi le

candidates.name: Limmat river cruise
candidates.price: Fr. 4.30, free with Zürich Card or a valid ZVV ticket for Zone 110
candidates.content: Offers views of the old town and Lake Zurich. Operates between April and October.

candidates.name: Theater am Neumarkt
candidates.content: Closer to downtown.

candidates.name: Swiss national day
candidates.content: 1st of August — Celebrations are carried out in many cities in the evenings and fireworks are launched at night. Watch them over the lake, or if you're experienced with safely launching fireworks yourself, you can buy them i

candidates.name: Cinema Arthouse Le Paris
candidates.content: Frequently changing arthouse movies; students get a discount.

candidates.name: Bar & Lounge 42
candidates.content: New York in the middle of Zurich. Exclusive whiskey, unique cocktails, premium liquors, snacks, a homemade gin and an elegant smoker's lounge with a broad selection of cigars.

candidates.name: Öpfelchammer
candidates.content: Not a real pub or café, they only serve wine or water. But if you succeed in climbing over the roof beams, you get a free glass of wine to drink hanging upside down and you can mark your name into the wood afterwards.

candidates.name: Barfussbar
candidates.content: During the day this is a public bath for women only. But at night (after 20:00) men are also allowed. It is a beautiful place to spend a warm summer night with a great view of Zurich.

candidates.name: Kasheme
candidates.content: This bar is all about good music. It features sometimes world famous DJs doing small mostly vinyl only sessions of funk, soul, disco and of course electronic music.

candidates.name: Kanonaegass Bar
candidates.content: Nice bar off Langstrasse with good drinks and good music. Bar is owned by 1990s electronic-music/trip-hop pioneer Richard Dorfmeister from Kruder & Dorfmeister.

candidates.name: Hive Club
candidates.content: Many rooms to wander through and listen to DJs from Switzerland and abroad. Sometimes offers nonstop parties during the weekends. Focus on Techno and House.

candidates.name: Helsinki
candidates.content: Small bar and club with nice atmosphere, especially in summer when the outdoor area is open. Live concerts most nights and safe haven for independent artists from all over Switzerland.

candidates.name: Gonzo
candidates.content: A basement club that generally plays no electronic music. Can be lots of fun but the queues are long and the door can be strict. Great on Wednesday (Hip-Hop) and Thursdays (students).

candidates.name: Rathauscafé
candidates.content: Coffee and a croissant in the morning, moving over to sparkling wine in the afternoon and early evening. Nice terrace in the summer. Mixed crowd, friendly service.

candidates.name: Bierhalle Wolf
candidates.content: A lively beer hall often with live music. In addition to the beer selection, they serve great local food.

candidates.name: Edi's Weinstube
candidates.content: nice wine bar in Niederdorf where you can get the cheapest okay wine in Zurich

candidates.name: Federal
candidates.content: A big brasserie-like bar inside the Main Station with a choice of 100 Swiss beers.

candidates.name: James Joyce bar
candidates.content: Where the writer used to drink. Now mostly frequented by bankers.

candidates.name: Oliver Twist
candidates.content: An Irish/British pub with a good atmosphere, and many English-speaking foreigners. Has English ales on draught.

candidates.name: Rheinfelder Bierhalle
candidates.content: In this huge and boisterous restaurant you get good value food and rich portions (only try the Jumbo Jumbo Cordon-Bleu when really hungry). Cheap beer. Service can range from very good to poor depending who is working that day.

candidates.name: Zeughauskeller
candidates.content: Offers hearty sausages, stews, rösti potato, etc., in a Brauhaus-like setting. Touristy, but good and large portions. Housed in a historical building, built in 1487.

candidates.name: Globus Bellevue
candidates.content: This relatively new branch of the Globus department store in the Bellevue near the Stadelhofen station is totally dedicated to food. There is a large eatery on the ground floor that serves various fusion-type foods (decent noodle

candidates.name: Outback Lodge
candidates.content: Unrelated to the U.S. Outback Steakhouse chain. Enjoy Aussie tucker like ostrich, kangaroo, and crocodile, as well as more conventional fare. Popular with locals as well as expats. Has a hopping bar scene (see Drink section). Ther

candidates.name: Le Dezaley
candidates.content: Traditional French-Swiss food from the French-speaking Kanton Waadt (Vaud). One of many fondue restaurants in Zurich.

candidates.name: Gambrinus
candidates.content: A typical Swiss restaurant with good food and cold beer. It is located in the Red Light District (Langstrasse) of Zurich and is not the ideal place to bring children or acquaintances. Gambrinus looks like a pub more than anything

candidates.name: Ah-Hua
candidates.content: Offers delicious Thai dishes to budget prices. Great pit-stop in a Langstrasse pub crawl.

candidates.name: Bank
candidates.content: Restaurant, café, bar and bakery in old bank. Mostly organic and Mediterranean food.

candidates.name: Swiss Chuchi
candidates.content: A kitchy place serving up classic Swiss fare, mainly for tourists. Serves fondue year round.

candidates.name: Tibits
candidates.content: The fast-food outlet of Hiltl, Europe's oldest vegetarian restaurant. Offers a nice self-service buffet of fresh veggies and fruit and a surprising variety. Try the freshly squeezed juices.

candidates.name: eCHo Restaurant
candidates.content: Traditional Swiss cuisine. Everything is prepared according to original recipes, and all products originate from the region.

candidates.name: Mesa Restaurant
candidates.content: Traditional kitchen with Catalan influences as one of the best restaurants in Zurich

candidates.name: Flohmarkt Bürkliplatz (Fleamarket)
candidates.content: Fairly relaxed yet large flea market with many interesting stalls.

candidates.name: Flohmarkt Kanzlei (Fleamarket)
candidates.content: A big flea market that hosts up to 400 stalls on busy days.

december.text: The train station and the connecting underground mall has shops, restaurants, and a grocery store which locals use when they need to do Sunday shopping, as it is not subject to the closing hours laws otherwise in force in the city. It also hosts a Christmas market and other events in the big entrance hall.
